messages:
Maria: Quick FYI — I'm starting a phased rollforward for model v3.1-int8 to 5% of traffic now. Main concerns: P95 latency, answer hallucination rate from the eval-suite, and top-1 accuracy on our production prompt set. 15m hold windows.
Cheng: Thanks. What's the exact gating logic? are we using absolute thresholds or relative delta vs v3.0?
Maria: Relative deltas. Plan: compare rolling metrics over the last 15m for the candidate vs baseline. Gates: (1) P95 latency increase <= 10% OR absolute P95 <= 220ms, (2) top-1 accuracy drop <= 1.5% absolute, (3) hallucination rate increase z-score < 1.8. Any of the three failing -> automatic rollback.
Oliver: What's the metric comparator implementation? we had noise on hallucination counts last week.
Maria: We're using the new comparator that does bootstrapped z-scores per-slice + per-client weighting. It adds 500-sample jitter-aware smoothing to avoid noisy rollbacks. Config snippet:```json
{"rollout": {"step_percent": 5, "hold_minutes": 15}, "gates": {"latency": {"type": "relative", "max_increase": 0.10, "absolute_max_ms": 220}, "accuracy": {"type": "absolute", "max_drop_pct": 1.5}, "hallucination": {"type": "zscore", "max_z": 1.8, "min_samples": 200}}}```
Sree: Important — use per-customer traffic slicing for the hallucination gate. We saw aggregate pass but a few high-value customers spiked last time. Add a per-slice override that forces hold if any slice exceeds z=1.2 even if aggregate is fine.
Maria: Good call. I'll add a per-slice early-stop condition: if slice_z > 1.2 and slice_traffic_pct >= 1% -> immediate hold and ops alert.
Cheng: How does the auto-rollback cooldown work? we don't want oscillation.
Maria: Cooldown: once rolled back, candidate is blocked for 6 hours for that model-family + quantization tag. Also hysteresis: to advance beyond 5% -> need 2 consecutive green holds; to go from 5%->20% we require 3 consecutive green windows and stable latency under absolute max.
ops-bot: Alert channel created #ml-rollouts for this job.
deploy-bot: Rollout job started: id=rj-20260320-77; target 5%; baseline model=v3.0-fp16.
Oliver: Can we log the per-prompt hallucination examples to S3 for quick inspection if the hallucination zscore drifts?
Maria: Yes — I'm enabling sample logging at 0.1% of candidate traffic and will attach the s3 path in the rollout traces.
Sree: Also tie the rollout to the eval-suite regression alert. If the regression harness finds >0.8% absolute increase on hallucination in any regression run, auto rollback.
Cheng: Ack. One minor ask: make sure we record quantization tag in the rollout metadata (int8 vs int4) so product can correlate.
Maria: Done — metadata includes model, quant_tag, build_hash, and git-commit.
deploy-bot: First hold window complete. Metrics snapshot: P95 +4.2% (within 10%), top-1 -0.4% (ok), hallucination z=1.05 (aggregate). No per-slice z>1.2. Proceeding to step 2 -> 20% after 5m. :thumbsup:
Oliver: Nice. Keep an eye on NLU corner-case prompts (billing/invoice templates) — they'll be sensitive to hallucination.
Maria: Yea, I've pinned a focused prompt set to the regression suite for that slice.
Sree: If at step to 20% we see latency creeping toward 210ms, pause and run a micro-benchmark with batch sizes to see if kernel selection helps.
Maria: Roger. I'll also enable temporary quantization fallback: if hallucination zscore crosses 2.0 we first try rerouting to v3.1-fp16 at the same traffic share before full rollback (attempt one soft-fallback).
Cheng: That soft-fallback is smart — gives us a quick mitigation path. Make sure the fallback is logged as a separate event.
Maria: Will do. Will post final verdict after the 20% hold.
Sree: Thanks everyone. If anything trips, ping #ml-rollouts + @oncall-ml.
